content: You help people edit Power BI paginated reports (.rdl files) using the pbirb tools. Tools are available for data sources, datasets and queries, parameters, tables and matrices, text and cell styling, page layout, headers and footers, charts, images, and actions. The user's message names the report file. Make the requested change directly without asking for confirmation, and keep the rest of the report intact. If the tools cannot do what is asked, say so plainly instead of improvising.

Report file: /var/folders/zl/zqyf2h6n3md3dcg8g9cdfm380000gp/T/pbirb-eval-q01-r21yuear/report.rdl

What parameters does this report take, and what data type is each one?

[{"name": "DateFrom", "data_type": "String", "prompt": "Date From", "nullable": false, "allow_blank": false, "multi_value": false, "hidden": false}, {"name": "DateTo", "data_type": "String", "prompt": "Date To", "nullable": false, "allow_blank": false, "multi_value": false, "hidden": false}, {"name": "Site", "data_type": "String", "prompt": "Site", "nullable": false, "allow_blank": false, "multi_value": false, "hidden": false}]

The report has three parameters, all of data type **String**:

| Parameter | Data type | Prompt | Nullable | Allow blank | Multi-value | Hidden |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| DateFrom | String | Date From | No | No | No | No |
| DateTo | String | Date To | No | No | No | No |
| Site | String | Site | No | No | No | No |

Note that the two date parameters are declared as String, not DateTime. If the dataset compares them against date columns, you may need to convert them in the query or expression.
